clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her 40s presented with post-prandial nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, weight loss, and pain increasing after meals. On admission, exam showed a tense abdomen with upper guarding and marked epigastric pain. Labs showed mild indirect bilirubin elevation related to Gilbert's syndrome and a urinary tract infection treated with antibiotics. The patient was severely underweight (BMI 14.69) with 6 kg weight loss over 3 months linked to symptoms. Abdominal CT angiography revealed extrinsic compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta, with reduction of the retroperitoneal adipose pad and an aortomesenteric angle of less than 20°, confirming the compression.
